name: SQL Injection
description: Untrusted input alters the structure of a SQL query.
consequences: Read, modify, or delete arbitrary database records; authentication bypass.
mitigation: Use parameterized queries / prepared statements; never concatenate input into SQL.

name: Cross-site Scripting (XSS)
description: Untrusted input is rendered in a page without escaping, running attacker script.
consequences: Session theft, account takeover, defacement, credential phishing.
mitigation: Escape output by context; use textContent; sanitize HTML; set a CSP.

name: OS Command Injection
description: Untrusted input is passed to a shell, running arbitrary commands.
consequences: Full remote code execution on the host.
mitigation: Avoid the shell; pass argument arrays; validate/allowlist input.

name: Path Traversal
description: User-controlled paths let an attacker read/write files outside the intended directory.
consequences: Disclosure of sensitive files (/etc/passwd), overwrite of config, RCE.
mitigation: Resolve and confirm the path stays within a safe base directory; allowlist names.

name: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
description: Secrets embedded in source are exposed to anyone with the code.
consequences: Account/API takeover, financial loss, lateral movement.
mitigation: Load secrets from environment or a secrets manager; rotate leaked keys.

name: Use of Hard-coded Password
description: A password constant is compiled into the application.
consequences: Anyone with the binary/source can authenticate.
mitigation: Store password hashes; read credentials from configuration.

name: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key
description: A signing/encryption key is embedded in code.
consequences: Attackers forge tokens or decrypt data.
mitigation: Generate keys at deploy time; store in a KMS/env.

name: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
description: Weak algorithms (DES, RC4) are used for protection.
consequences: Data can be decrypted or forged.
mitigation: Use vetted algorithms (AES-GCM, SHA-256+).

name: Use of Weak Hash
description: Fast/broken hashes (MD5, SHA-1) are used for passwords.
mitigation: Use bcrypt/scrypt/argon2 with a salt.

name: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
description: Deserializing attacker data instantiates arbitrary objects.
mitigation: Use safe formats (JSON); yaml.safe_load; never pickle untrusted data.

name: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
description: The server fetches a user-supplied URL, reaching internal services.
consequences: Access to cloud metadata, internal APIs, port scanning.
mitigation: Allowlist hosts; block private IP ranges; disable redirects.

name: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
description: State-changing requests lack an anti-forgery token.
consequences: Actions performed as the victim without consent.
mitigation: Use CSRF tokens and SameSite cookies.

name: Improper Authentication
description: Authentication can be bypassed or is not enforced.
consequences: Unauthorized access to accounts and data.
mitigation: Enforce auth on every sensitive route; verify credentials server-side.

name: Missing Authentication for Critical Function
description: A sensitive endpoint is reachable without authentication.
mitigation: Require auth/authorization decorators on admin and mutating routes.

name: Missing Authorization
description: No check that the caller may access the specific resource.
mitigation: Verify ownership/role on every object access.

name: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key (IDOR)
description: An object id from the request is trusted without an ownership check.
consequences: Read/modify other users' records by changing an id.
mitigation: Scope queries to the authenticated user; use unguessable ids.

name: Exposure of Sensitive Information
description: Sensitive data is returned where it should not be.
mitigation: Return only needed fields; strip secrets/PII from responses.

name: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File
description: Secrets or PII are written to logs.
mitigation: Redact sensitive fields before logging.

name: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information
description: Sensitive data is stored unencrypted.
mitigation: Encrypt at rest; hash passwords.

name: Missing Encryption of Sensitive Data
description: Sensitive data is transmitted/stored without encryption.
mitigation: Use TLS; encrypt stored secrets.

name: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
description: Uploaded files are not validated and can be executed.
mitigation: Allowlist extensions/MIME; store outside the web root.

name: Open Redirect
description: A user-controlled redirect target is not validated.
mitigation: Allowlist redirect destinations.

name: XML External Entity (XXE)
description: An XML parser resolves external entities.
mitigation: Disable DTD/external entity resolution.

name: Code Injection
description: Untrusted input is evaluated as code.
mitigation: Never eval input; use safe parsers.

name: Improper Output Neutralization for Logs (Log Injection)
description: Unsanitized input in logs forges or corrupts log entries.
mitigation: Strip newlines/encode input before logging.

name: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information
description: Error handlers leak stack traces, secrets, or prompts.
mitigation: Return generic errors; log details server-side only.

name: Improper Certificate Validation
description: TLS certificate verification is disabled.
mitigation: Enable verification; pin certs where appropriate.

name: Use of Insufficiently Random Values
description: Predictable randomness is used for security tokens.
mitigation: Use a CSPRNG (secrets, crypto.randomBytes).

name: Active Debug Code
description: Debug mode is enabled in production.
consequences: RCE via the debugger, information disclosure.
mitigation: Disable debug in production builds.

name: Sensitive Cookie Without HttpOnly Flag
description: Session cookies are readable by JavaScript.
mitigation: Set HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite on session cookies.

javascript.fixed: res.cookie("sid", id, { httpOnly: true, secure: true, sameSite: "strict" })

name: Permissive Cross-domain Policy (CORS)
description: CORS allows any origin together with credentials.
consequences: Authenticated data readable by any site.
mitigation: Allowlist specific origins; avoid * with credentials.

name: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature
description: A JWT/signature is trusted without verification.
mitigation: Verify signatures; reject alg:none.
